questions.prompt: A lift of mass $600\text{ kg}$ carries a crate of mass $200\text{ kg}$. The lift is raised vertically with an upward acceleration of $1.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the tension in the lift cable and calculate the normal reaction exerted by the floor of the lift on the crate.

questions.prompt: A passenger of mass $70\text{ kg}$ stands on the floor of a lift of mass $430\text{ kg}$. The lift moves downwards and is brought to rest with a constant deceleration of $1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the tension in the cable during this deceleration, and determine the normal reaction exerted by the lift floor on the passenger.

questions.prompt: A crate of mass $40\text{ kg}$ rests on the floor of a lift of mass $360\text{ kg}$. The lift accelerates downwards, and the normal reaction exerted by the floor on the crate is $320\text{ N}$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the downward acceleration of the lift, and find the tension in the hoisting cable.

questions.prompt: A block of mass $5\text{ kg}$ is suspended from the ceiling of a lift by a light inextensible string. When the lift accelerates vertically upwards, the tension in the string is $65\text{ N}$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the acceleration of the lift, and determine the tension in the string when the lift accelerates vertically downwards with the same magnitude of acceleration.

questions.prompt: A man of mass $80\text{ kg}$ stands on a bathroom scale placed on the floor of a lift. The lift accelerates vertically upwards from rest at $1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and subsequently moves upwards at a constant speed.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the reading on the scale while the lift is accelerating upwards, and state the scale reading while the lift travels at constant speed.

questions.prompt: A lift and its passengers have a total mass of $1200\text{ kg}$. The supporting cable can withstand a maximum tension of $15000\text{ N}$ without snapping.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum upward acceleration the lift can have without exceeding this cable tension, and find the speed reached by the lift starting from rest after accelerating at this maximum rate for $3\text{ s}$.

questions.prompt: A lift of mass $500\text{ kg}$ carries a passenger of mass $60\text{ kg}$. The lift ascends vertically from rest.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: During the initial phase, the lift accelerates upwards at $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$. Find the tension in the lift cable and the normal reaction on the passenger.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Near the top floor, the ascending lift decelerates at $1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to come to rest. Calculate the new cable tension and the new reaction on the passenger.

questions.prompt: A goods lift of mass $450\text{ kg}$ carries two crates, $A$ and $B$, resting on the horizontal floor. Crate $A$ of mass $30\text{ kg}$ is placed on top of crate $B$ of mass $50\text{ kg}$. The lift ascends with an upward acceleration of $1.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the tension in the lift cable during this motion.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the contact force exerted by crate $B$ on crate $A$, and determine the contact force exerted by the lift floor on crate $B$.

questions.prompt: A passenger lift of mass $600\text{ kg}$ carrying a person of mass $80\text{ kg}$ ascends vertically through a total height of $21\text{ m}$. The journey consists of three stages: acceleration from rest at $1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ for $2\text{ s}$, followed by motion at constant speed for $5\text{ s}$, and finally uniform deceleration of $1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to rest.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the tension in the lift cable during each of the three stages of motion.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the normal reaction exerted by the floor on the passenger during the acceleration stage and during the deceleration stage.

questions.prompt: A lift of mass $M\text{ kg}$ carries a crate of mass $120\text{ kg}$. The lift descends vertically from rest, accelerating downwards at $0.8\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to a steady speed, and later decelerates to rest at $1.6\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the normal reaction exerted by the floor on the crate during the downward acceleration phase, and during the downward deceleration phase.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Given that the tension in the cable during the downward deceleration phase is $8120\text{ N}$, determine the mass $M$ of the lift, and calculate the tension in the cable during the downward acceleration phase.

questions.prompt: A lift cage $A$ of mass $320\text{ kg}$ contains a box of mass $80\text{ kg}$. The cage is connected by a light cable passing over a smooth fixed pulley to a counterweight $B$ of mass $600\text{ kg}$. The system is released from rest with both vertical sections taut.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration of the system and find the tension in the cable.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the normal reaction exerted by the floor of the lift on the box during motion, and calculate the speed of the box after the lift has ascended a distance of $2.25\text{ m}$ from rest.

questions.prompt: A lift of mass $400\text{ kg}$ contains a parcel $P$ of mass $8\text{ kg}$ suspended from the ceiling by a light string, and a crate $Q$ of mass $52\text{ kg}$ resting on the floor. The lift ascends vertically.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: While the lift is accelerating upwards, the tension in the string supporting parcel $P$ is $96\text{ N}$. Find the acceleration of the lift, the normal reaction exerted on crate $Q$, and the tension in the main hoisting cable.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Later in the ascent, the lift decelerates uniformly to rest. During this deceleration, the normal reaction on crate $Q$ is $416\text{ N}$. Calculate the magnitude of the deceleration, find the tension in the string supporting parcel $P$, and calculate the cable tension.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: If the lift was ascending at a speed of $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at the beginning of the deceleration phase, find the time taken to come to rest, and calculate the distance travelled during deceleration.

questions.prompt: A mine cage of mass $800\text{ kg}$ carrying miners of total mass $400\text{ kg}$ is being lowered down a vertical shaft. The cage is initially lowered from rest with a constant downward acceleration of $1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ for $4\text{ s}$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the tension in the cable during this descent, and calculate the total normal reaction exerted by the floor of the cage on the miners.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: At $t = 4\text{ s}$, the cable suddenly breaks. The cage falls freely under gravity for $0.5\text{ s}$ before emergency guide-rail brakes engage. Show that the normal reaction on the miners during free fall is zero, and find the downward speed of the cage at the instant the brakes engage.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The emergency guide-rail brakes exert a total constant upward retarding force of $18000\text{ N}$ on the cage. Calculate the deceleration of the cage, the distance it descends before coming to rest, and the normal reaction on the miners during braking.
